youtube.title: What is the flattest country in the world? Its peak is 5 metres high 📏
youtube.description:
Netherlands, Denmark or the third one? One nation's highest natural point would fit under a two-storey house, and most of its land sits about a metre and a half above the sea. Its capital is ringed by a wall, and its government once held a cabinet meeting underwater to make the point.
Guess before the map lights up, then see the three high points side by side and the wall that keeps the capital dry.
Which did you pick?

research.topic: Flattest / lowest country: Maldives — highest natural point about 2.4 m (CIA: 5 m on Vilingili, 8th tee of a golf course), average ground elevation ~1.5 m, 1,190 coral islands in 26 atolls; the Netherlands' highest point Vaalserberg 322 m, Denmark's Møllehøj 171 m; Malé protected by a 3 m sea wall built with Japanese aid after the 1987 floods; 17 October 2009 President Nasheed's cabinet met underwater at Girifushi to sign a declaration ahead of the Copenhagen climate summit.

myths.myth: The Netherlands is the flattest country — a quarter of it lies below sea level.
myths.reality: Much of the Netherlands is below sea level, but its highest point is 322 m; the Maldives' highest natural point is a few metres and no land rises above about 5 m.

landscape.our_gap: Clips either tour Maldives resorts or run a 'countries that will disappear' list; nobody puts the three high points side by side, measures the Malé wall against the average and shows the underwater cabinet on a moving map as a quiz.
